blocking_issues.issue: FINDINGS.md Validation section misstates swe_bench_crossed convergence: 'all repro fits and swe crossed pass globally (r_hat <= 1.003, ESS >= 780 headline)'. The file outputs/swe_bench_crossed.diagnostics.json shows global max r_hat = 1.0124 and min ESS 597 (nuisance z_item), which does NOT pass globally at the 1.01 gate; the parenthetical numbers (1.003, 780) are its HEADLINE stats (sigma_item). The elevated-r_hat list '1.017/1.037/1.013 (cybench/gdm/boolq)' also omits swe's 1.0124. Fix the sentence to put swe crossed in the nuisance-z group with its headline stats stated separately.

Two FINDINGS claims are not traceable to any output file, violating the stated output contract: (a) Finding 1's pre-dedup '87 replicate groups (222 runs >= 10 samples), mostly sd=0' - reviewer reproduced it exactly from raw parquet, so it is correct, but save a pre-dedup replicate-group CSV (and note the >=10 threshold differs from the >=20 used post-dedup); (b) the Validation claim that swe_repro's posterior is 'stable across target_accept 0.95/0.97/0.99 reruns' - reviewer's independent reruns confirm it (sigma_run 0.129/0.122 vs 0.118, overlapping HDIs), but the rerun diagnostics must be saved as an artifact or the sentence dropped in favour of the standard boundary-funnel justification alone.

suggestions: S1: The crossed_binomial cell likelihood ignores the run-level overdispersion the experiment itself measures (sigma_run ~ 0.57 logit on cybench). Ability HDIs and especially the discrimination-ratio denominators are therefore optimistic. The caveat exists but is not connected to the affected metrics; either state explicitly that disc ratios are upper bounds conditional on the model, or run a beta-binomial-cell (or run-random-effect) sensitivity fit for one benchmark.

S2: Synthetic recovery for the crossed model uses a milder regime (rho ~ 0.21, sigma_item 1.2, 8 models, no all-solve/no-solve items) than the real data (rho 0.68, 45 models, many extreme items - the very regime that produces the nuisance-z r_hat trouble). Recovery also simulates from the fitted model, so it cannot detect the S1 misspecification. Add one harsher synthetic scenario.

S3: The null synthetic check 'pass if posterior mean <= 0.06' observed 0.0599 - a razor-thin pass against a threshold that looks post hoc. Prefer a prior-vs-posterior concentration criterion (e.g. posterior mass below 0.1 vs prior mass) so the null check is principled.

S4: boolq's discrimination ratio (112, probability scale with tiny eval-level SEs) sits in the same league-table column as logit-scale ratios; it is footnoted in FINDINGS but the CSV itself carries no scale annotation - add a scale column or footnote to health_league_table.csv.
S5: abilities_forest.png strips provider prefixes, producing duplicate y-labels (two 'Mistral-Large-2411' on cybench, two 'oak' on gdm); keep a provider disambiguator.
S6: diagnostics.json 'model' field concatenates model+tag ('boolq_normalboolq_normal') - cosmetic bridge issue, worth fixing for the synthesis report.
strengths: The duplicate-ingest discovery (31-51% of public sample rows are literal copies) is a genuinely valuable warehouse-hygiene finding, correctly diagnosed and correctly handled.
Exclusion accounting is exact; error/limit policy is the right call for agentic tasks and is justified rather than asserted.
Fixed model effects to dodge the few-group shrinkage trap, non-centred hierarchies, and centring-adjusted synthetic truth estimands are all technically correct.

Headline-metric convergence gating (derived_diagnostics.csv) is the right response to nuisance-parameter r_hat inflation, and every per-parameter number quoted in FINDINGS matched the reviewer's recomputation from the idata files.
Honest observational framing throughout; no causal claims; every headline number carries a 94% HDI.
verdict_summary: High-quality, near-approvable work. All spot-checked numbers trace or reproduce exactly; models, priors, synthetic recovery and hygiene policies are sound and honestly reported. Two must-fix items remain: one false convergence sentence about swe_bench_crossed (contradicted by the project's own diagnostics file) and two untraceable-though-correct claims that need saved artifacts. Fix those and this is ready for SoE.
